answer: Because the pearl index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the knoll audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 233 answers need 233 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the pulse identifier and voids the later submissions, and hence the operator burns for 233 runs and collects one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
